arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 4/5 — her number is in his phone. Mon Nov 9 she drew a running dog on his foam and left at the end of her shift. Today: she hears about the wink and draws a winking basil leaf, on the house; reminds him of the Moshe photo Saturday. Next: the photo about Sat Nov 14, then a first date.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 2/3 — recovering by the sink with Dana's sprout ('Moshe's roommate'); he touched a fresh leaf Mon Nov 9. Next: visibly thriving, the photo for Dana.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 9: the client loved it; the wink sold for 1,000 extra (he asked 1,200); main logo files sent; invoice at thirty days. Today: which eye (left, same price, a blink is another job) and a rough preview a day early. Next: final wink files Wed Nov 11 night before the concert, then getting paid.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: Phoned him three times Monday; said she'll celebrate with him at the Pump House Wednesday. Next: Penguins can Fly Wed Nov 11 (the engine picks his company).

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: 'Yes, and' now leaks into everything: Gadi, Lior's deposit, Moti's committee. Next: lesson 2 Thu Nov 12 at 17:00, then the beer for Tomer (now partly paid by the committee, receipt required).

arcs.title: The wider circle
arcs.stage: Mon: Avi brought leftover falafel at night; Tomer borrowed the drill and wants to hear about the penguins Wednesday; Hagit at the ticket window; Sivan and Michal at the gym. Today: Lior (half up front), Mr. Zelig (a wink is a secret), Moti (fees, a beer for Tomer, Boaz calls him 'the quiet one'). Next: Boaz's poker invitation Nov 19-21.

beats.goal: Ishai starts the winking-chickpea animation (three frames, due to Gadi Wednesday night). Gadi texts a new question from the client Ruti: which eye winks? Ishai phones him and, with improv's 'yes, and', keeps it to one eye for the agreed thousand; a second eye would be another job. Then he draws the frames with Falafel at his feet.
beats.teaser: The client has a new question about the chickpea's wink
beats.forceText: At his desk Ishai draws three chickpea faces in a row. Gadi texts about which eye should wink; Ishai answers 'the left one, same price'.

forceLines.say: Left eye. One eye, one wink, one thousand. Done.

forceCommentary.say: A chickpea with a dominant eye. Science has peaked.

message.say: Ruti again. Which eye winks? Left or right? She says it matters. She's left-handed. Don't ask.

moments.text: Morning light on the desk. Ishai, coffee in hand, has three empty frames open on the screen when his phone buzzes; Falafel lifts his head from the rug.

lines.say: Which eye. Which eye? It's a chickpea. It doesn't have a left.
Okay. Calm. Yes, and. Call him.

commentary.say: A left-handed client wants a left-eyed chickpea. Respect the vision.
Day two of the wink. It has not winked yet.

moments.text: Ishai paces between the desk and the kitchen counter with the phone at his ear, one hand drawing small circles in the air.

lines.say: So? Left or right? She's waiting. She's always waiting.
Left. People read from the right here, so the eye lands last. It feels like a goodbye.
That's very clever. Did you just make that up?
Yes. And it's also true.
Fine. And what if she wants both eyes later? For a blink?
Then that's a blink. A blink is a different job.
A different job. You've got a price list now? Since yesterday?
Since yesterday. It's a short list. One line.
Wednesday night, Ishai. Not Thursday morning. Wednesday.
Wednesday night. Before ten. I have a concert at eight.
A concert. Freelancers. Send it before the drummer starts.
Before the drummer. Promise. Bye, Gadi.

commentary.say: 'A blink is a different job.' Somebody frame that and hang it in Sababa Creative.
He has a price list. One line long. Still longer than my patience.

update.memory: Ishai now says no to free extras: left eye only, a blink would be another job. Wink files due Wednesday night before his concert.

moments.text: Back at the desk Ishai draws the chickpea three times: eyes open, the left eye half shut, the wink. He flips between them fast; Falafel tilts his head at the screen.

lines.say: Open. Half. Wink. Falafel, look. It likes you.
Too creepy. Softer eyebrow. Again.

commentary.say: The dog tilted his head. That's a yes from the focus group.
Three frames. He'll redraw the eyebrow forty times. I've seen this before.

beats.goal: After the lecture Ishai has lunch at Cafe Nahat. Dana asks how the presentation went and hears about the wink. Lior, still writing the same novel, brings up the book cover (2,000 'when it's finished'); for the first time Ishai asks for half up front, kindly, and Lior has to think about whether the book will ever be finished. Dana's next cup has a basil leaf with one eye shut. No date talk yet; the Moshe photo is still due Saturday.
beats.teaser: Lior wants his book cover, and Ishai names his terms
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Ishai tells Lior the book cover needs half up front. Lior looks at his laptop for a long time. Dana brings a cup with a winking basil leaf.

forceLines.say: Half up front, Lior. Then the cover waits for the book, not the other way.
Half of a book that isn't finished. That's philosophy.

forceCommentary.say: Three days of improv and he's invoicing novelists. Who IS he?

moments.text: Cafe Nahat at lunchtime. Ishai sits at the corner table with his jacket on the chair. Dana sets down his coffee and doesn't leave right away.

lines.say: So. The presentation. Did the chickpea survive?
It survived. Now the client wants it to wink.
A winking chickpea. That's either cute or a lawsuit.
Cute. For a thousand shekels extra. I said the number out loud.
Out loud? With your mouth? I'm impressed.
I almost said sorry first. I swallowed it.
Good. Sorry is for when you spill something. Like Lior.
How's Lior's novel?
Same page since August. I've read it upside down from the counter.
Is it good?
The first sentence is excellent. Ask him about the second.

commentary.say: She stayed at the table. She had other tables. She stayed.
Same page since August. Lior, I relate on a spiritual level.

update.memory: Ishai sold a winking chickpea for a thousand extra and almost said sorry first. He swallowed it. Moshe photo still due Saturday.

moments.text: Lior drags his chair over from the window table with his laptop under his arm, the same document open as always.

lines.say: Ishai. The cover. I've been thinking. A man, a door, maybe fog.
Fog is good. Lior, how far is the book?
Far. Close. It depends on the chapter. Chapter one is perfect.
Then here's how I work now. Half up front. A thousand.
Up front? For a cover of a book that isn't finished?
Yes. And the cover will make you finish it. You'll want to see it on a shelf.
That's... manipulative. And true. Who taught you that?
A woman named Yael. Thursdays. Long story.
I'll think about it. I'll write about it, actually. Chapter two.
Chapter two. Finally. I'll take that as progress.
Don't tell Dana. She reads my screen from the counter.

commentary.say: 'Half up front.' Lior just aged a year. The book aged ten.
A deposit to finish a novel. He invented a business model in one sentence.

update.memory: Ishai asked for half up front for my cover: a thousand. Said the cover will make me finish. Annoyingly right. Chapter two, maybe.

moments.text: Dana brings a second coffee he didn't order. On the foam is a basil leaf with a tiny face, one eye shut. She puts it down without a word and waits.

lines.say: Is that... is the leaf winking at me?
It's practising. For the chickpea. Professional courtesy.
I didn't order a second one.
It's on the house. Don't tell Lior, he'll want a deposit.
You heard that?
The whole cafe heard it. Lior typed for ten minutes after. A record.
How's Moshe's baby doing, by the way? The sprout? Is it his, or yours?
It's Moshe's roommate. Saturday I want a photo of both. Don't forget.
Saturday. I have a reminder. Two reminders.
One is confidence. Two is... cute. Drink it before it stops winking.

commentary.say: A winking leaf. On the house. If that is not a love letter, nothing is.
Two reminders for one photo. A man with a system.

update.memory: Gave Ishai a winking basil leaf on the house. He asked Lior for a deposit. Moshe and the sprout photo due Saturday; he has two reminders.

beats.goal: Ishai takes Falafel for an afternoon walk in the park with his sketchbook to test the wink on paper. On the bench Mr. Zelig is lecturing the pigeons. He looks at the drawings and says birds don't wink, they blink sideways, and a wink is a secret between two people. Ishai likes that and keeps it for the animation. Zelig asks Falafel his opinion.
beats.teaser: Mr. Zelig has opinions about winking. So do the pigeons.
beats.forceText: On the park bench Mr. Zelig studies Ishai's chickpea drawings and tells him a wink is a secret between two people. Falafel watches the pigeons.

forceLines.say: A wink is a secret between two people. The pigeons know nothing about it.

forceCommentary.say: Life advice from the man who negotiates with pigeons. And it was good. I'm upset.

moments.text: The park in the cool afternoon sun. Ishai sits at the end of the bench with a sketchbook on his knee and Falafel on the red leash; at the other end Mr. Zelig scatters crumbs and talks to the pigeons.

lines.say: No. You had yours. Let the grey one eat. He's had a bad week.
Afternoon, Mr. Zelig.
The young man with the wolf. Sit, sit, you're already sitting. What are you drawing?
A chickpea. It has to wink. For an app.
Let me see. Hm. That one looks like it has sand in its eye.
That's the middle frame. Half closed.
Birds don't wink, you know. They blink sideways. A skin, like a curtain.
Sideways? I didn't know that.
Nobody knows. Nobody asks the birds. I ask.
What do they say?
Mostly 'bread'. They're not deep.

commentary.say: Mr. Zelig, art critic. Harsh. Fair. Smells faintly of crumbs.
'They're not deep.' He's been talking to them for years and that's his verdict.

moments.text: Mr. Zelig holds the sketchbook at arm's length and squints; Falafel stares at the pigeons, trembling, sitting perfectly still.

lines.say: A wink is a secret between two people. You know that? Not a joke. A secret.
A secret. So the chickpea and the customer share something.
Exactly. Your food is coming, and only you two know. Make the eye slower.
Slower. Hold the wink a bit longer.
My wife winked at me once across a wedding. Forty-one years it held.
That's a long wink.
The longest. Your wolf, does he agree? Ask him.
Falafel? What do you think? He thinks pigeons.
Everybody thinks pigeons. Go, draw. Slower, remember.
Slower. Thank you, Mr. Zelig. Really.

commentary.say: He came for a sketch and left with a forty-one-year wink. I need a minute.
Falafel has been frozen for six minutes. The pigeons are winning.

update.memory: The young man with the wolf draws a winking chickpea. I told him: a wink is a secret, make it slower. He listened. Rare.

beats.goal: Moti from apartment 1, head of the building committee, comes up the stairs with his folder to collect Ishai's committee fees, including the share for the stair light. Ishai pays, and, with 'yes, and', points out that Tomer fixed the hallway light for free, so the committee could buy Tomer a beer from petty cash. Moti grumbles about receipts and agrees to one beer. He mentions, in passing, that Boaz from apartment 2 calls Ishai 'the quiet one'. Mrs. Levi's game show starts shouting through her door at 19:30.
beats.teaser: The building committee comes knocking, folder in hand
beats.forceText: In the corridor Moti from the committee collects Ishai's fees from his folder and, after some grumbling, agrees the committee owes Tomer a beer.

forceLines.say: One beer. From petty cash. I need a receipt, Ishai. A receipt.
Yes, and I'll get him to sign it.

forceCommentary.say: A building committee paying in beer. Finally, a government I believe in.

moments.text: Evening in the stairwell. Ishai opens his door to a knock; Moti from apartment 1 stands there in a cardigan with a thick plastic folder and a pen behind his ear. Falafel pushes his nose past Ishai's knee.

lines.say: Good evening. Committee. Apartment four, you're two months behind. Plus the stair light.
Moti, hi. Right. Sorry, I... no. Not sorry. How much?
Two months is two hundred forty. The stair light, thirty-five. Two seventy-five.
Two hundred forty, fine. But the stair light, my friend Tomer fixed that. For free.
I know. I wrote it in the group. The committee thanked him officially.
With a message. He's an electrician. He works for money, usually.
The thirty-five was for the bulb, Ishai. Bulbs cost money.
He brought his own bulb. And tape from 1990. He was proud of the tape.
Hm. The tape I saw. Very old tape.
So yes, I'll pay. And the committee buys Tomer a beer. Thursday. The Black Candle.
A beer. From the building's money. Do you know how this looks?

commentary.say: He started a sorry and cancelled it mid-air. Yael, that's your homework working.
Moti carries that folder like it holds nuclear codes. It holds the bulb budget.

moments.text: Moti opens the folder on his knee and writes slowly while Ishai counts notes from his wallet; behind apartment 5's door a TV game show starts and Mrs. Levi shouts an answer at it.

lines.say: Fine. One beer. Petty cash. I need a receipt, Ishai. A real receipt.
Yes, and Tomer will sign it. He'll love signing something.
Don't let him write jokes on it. The last receipt from apartment seven had a drawing.
I can't promise anything about Tomer.
Two hundred forty. Received. You're a good tenant. Quiet. Boaz says it too.
Boaz from two? The bus driver? He says I'm quiet?
'The quiet one from four.' It's a compliment. In this building, quiet is rare.
Mrs. Levi seems to agree. Listen to her.
She's right about one answer a week. Good night, Ishai. Receipt!
Receipt. Good night, Moti.

commentary.say: 'The quiet one from four.' Boaz is taking notes. Why is Boaz taking notes?
Mrs. Levi just shouted 'PARIS' at a question about cheese. Love her.

update.memory: Ishai paid two months. Says Tomer fixed the light for free, so the committee owes Tomer a beer: one, petty cash, with a receipt. Quiet tenant, Boaz agrees.

beats.goal: Ishai finishes a first test of the wink with Zelig's advice (a slower wink) and sends Gadi a rough preview a day early. Gadi texts back, grudgingly impressed. Ishai shows the wink to Moshe and Falafel and then stops working, because tomorrow is the lecture, the final files and the concert.
beats.teaser: The chickpea winks for the first time. Gadi reacts.
beats.forceText: At his desk Ishai plays the chickpea's slow wink on a loop, sends Gadi a preview, and gets back: 'It winked at me. I didn't like it. Ruti will love it.'

forceLines.say: He didn't like it. That's Gadi for 'it's good'.

forceCommentary.say: The chickpea winked. I felt seen. I need to lie down.

moments.text: Late evening, only the desk lamp on. On the laptop the chickpea winks on a loop: open, slowly half closed, the wink held a beat, then open again. Ishai leans back and watches it ten times.

lines.say: Slower. He was right. The old man was right.
Okay, Gadi. Rough preview. A day early. Don't get used to it.

commentary.say: He's watching a chickpea wink on loop at night. This is what love looks like in 2026.
He's using the pigeon man's notes. Credit Mr. Zelig in the files.

message.say: It winked at me. I didn't like it. Ruti will love it. Final files tomorrow night. Go to your concert.

moments.text: His phone lights up next to the keyboard. Ishai reads it, laughs out loud and spins once in the squeaky chair.

lines.say: He didn't like it. That's Gadi for 'it's very good'.
Falafel! Gadi approved! In his language.

commentary.say: 'I didn't like it.' From Gadi that's a medal and a hug.
'Go to your concert.' Gadi just gave him the night off. Who are these people now?

moments.text: Ishai carries the laptop to the kitchen counter and holds it up to Moshe and the little sprout so they can see the wink; Falafel follows and sits, watching the screen.

lines.say: Moshe, look. It winks. Slowly. It's a secret between two people.
Three people. And a dog. Okay, it's not a secret anymore.

commentary.say: He showed the chickpea to Moshe first. Correct order. Moshe outranks everyone.
Laptop closed at a reasonable hour. Tomorrow: lecture, files, and penguins.

hosts: Tuesday. No holiday, no presentation. Just a man and a chickpea that must learn to wink.
The wink is three frames. He'll draw thirty. It's how he loves.
Lecture at eleven. The War of Jenkins' Ear. Yes, an ear. Started a war. History is unwell.
Gadi said 'good job' yesterday. Oren is still in recovery.
I am fine. I simply need Gadi to stay mean so the universe makes sense.
Falafel has a schedule now: breakfast, walk, rug, judging, walk, rug.
Moshe grew a leaf. A real one. Oren saw it on the monitor and stood up.
The sprout still has no name. Oren is drafting a shortlist. It's laminated.
Tomorrow at eight: Penguins can Fly at the Pump House. Science disagrees. We're going.
Hagit says eight sharp. Hagit has never said anything that wasn't sharp.
Noa promised to celebrate Wednesday. Tomer said maybe. Tomer always says maybe.
Thursday: improv lesson two. And a beer for Tomer. The man owes beer like a bank.
Cafe Nahat at lunch. Lior has been on chapter one since August. Respect the craft.
Lior's novel has a first sentence. A great one. And then the fog rolls in.
Mr. Zelig feeds the pigeons in order of who had a bad week. That's a system.
Mrs. Levi's game show at seven thirty. She shouts answers. Some are even to that show.
The building committee has a folder. The folder has a pen. The pen has power.
Ishai's price list has one line now. That's one more than yesterday.
Cool and clear today. He'll wear the jacket and then carry it.
Dana draws on foam. Ishai draws on screens. It's practically a joint exhibition.
He hasn't said sorry since nine this morning. We're tracking it. Don't jinx it.
The squeaky chair squeaks in three notes. It's become the show's theme song.
Fun fact: a chickpea has no eyelids. Ishai is overcoming biology.
If the chickpea winks at you in the app, you're welcome. Ishai did that.
Moshe's roommate. That's what we're calling the sprout until Oren finishes his list.
Saturday is photo day. Dana asked for Moshe. Ishai set two reminders. Plural.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Tuesday, and the city woke up cold and clear. Wear the jacket, take it off at noon.
Ten degrees at dawn, twenty-two by lunch. Tel Aviv, the city that dresses in layers.
Tuesday is the day nobody writes songs about. Let's fix that. Here's one anyway.
A listener asks: can you charge extra for a small thing? Yes. Small things take the longest.
Gas truck on the side streets this morning. If it plays music, it's not the ice cream man.
Somebody in Florentin says his neighbour practises piano at four every day. Same piece. Two years.
Traffic on the Ayalon: slow. Traffic on Herzl Street: one scooter and a very confident pigeon.
Tomorrow night, the old Pump House across the park has live music. Bring earplugs or a friend.
Fact of the day: a pigeon can recognise faces. So be nice. They talk.
School's out at half past one. Drivers, look twice. Kids, look once at least.
It's the evening hour on Radio Herzl. Put the kettle on, the day is almost over.
Weather tomorrow: clear again. No excuse not to go out Wednesday night.
To the man who sings along from apartment four: we can't hear you, but we believe in you.

zelig: The grey one had a bad week. Let him eat first.
Sideways. They blink sideways. Nobody asks.
Forty-one years, one wink. Try that, pigeons.
Not you. You had bread on Sunday. I remember.
michal: Ten more. Nine. Who's counting, I'm counting.
My cat would judge this form.
Run club Friday. I'll send it to the group. I won't go.
sivan: Eleven point five. Not bad. Not good.
Heart rate one-forty. Still talking. Too slow.
The husky guy. Not today. Pity.
lior: Chapter one. Again. It's perfect. That's the problem.
Half up front. Half of what?
A man, a door, fog. That's a cover. That's a life.
kobi: Tuesday numbers: four, nine, twelve. Not a system. A feeling.
First beer is for thinking. Second is for answers.
Ishai? Haven't seen him since the scooter talk. Buy it, man.

street: ...he said the bus comes at ten, I said which ten...
...my mother wants me to fix her phone, so I gave her mine...
...the gas truck plays Für Elise, I can't hear it anymore without panic...
...two shekels more for amba? Since when, Avi?...
market: ...these tomatoes are from Tuesday. Which Tuesday?...
...he wanted a discount for being a regular, he came once...
...you smell the za'atar? That's the real one, not the dust...
...I said one kilo, he gave me one and a half and a speech...
park: ...the duck has a name, but he won't tell anyone...
...my dog only listens in English, it's very annoying...
...I'm walking, not jogging, it's a choice...
...the old man said the pigeons voted against me...
cafe: ...she draws a heart for everyone, don't feel special...
...my thesis is basically done, except for writing it...
...oat milk, no, almond, no, just a regular, sorry...
...the guy by the window has been on page one since summer...

chat.say: Reminder: committee fees for September and October. I'm coming round this evening with the folder.
Can I pay in December? I'm emotionally in December already.
The gas truck is here. Whoever ordered, go down, he's playing that song again.
Who left a bicycle on the first floor landing? I nearly flew.
The piano upstairs is getting better. Slightly. Keep going.
My show starts. If you hear shouting, it's the questions, not me.
Thank you to apt 4. Committee will buy the electrician one beer. One. Receipt please.
